questions.problem:
Let $a$ be a positive integer. Construct an expression that gives the last digit of $a.$

$$
a{{field-1}}{{field-2}}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Let ${d}_{3},$ ${d}_{2},$ and ${d}_{1}$ be the last three digits of the number $a:$ 

$$
a=…{d}_{3}{d}_{2}{d}_{1}
$$

Then, $a$ can be written in expanded form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⋯+100{d}_{3}+10{d}_{2}+{d}_{1} \\  & =10(⋯+10{d}_{3}+{d}_{2})+{d}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the residue of $a$ modulo $10:$

$$
\begin{aligned}a & ≡10(⋯+10{d}_{3}+{d}_{2})+{d}_{1} &  & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡0\cdot (⋯+10{d}_{3}+{d}_{2})+{d}_{1} &  & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡0+{d}_{1} &  & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡{d}_{1} &  & (\text{mod}\,10)\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that ${d}_{1}$ is the last digit of $a.$

Therefore, the expression that gives the last digit of $a$ is the following:

$$
a\,\text{mod}\,10
$$

questions.worked_solution:
The residue of $33$ modulo $6$ is the integer $0\le r<6$ such that

$$
33≡r\,(\text{mod}\,6).
$$

**Method 1**

To find the residue $r,$ we need to write $33$ as an integer multiple of $6,$ plus the residue $r.$

We note that $33≡3\,(\text{mod}\,6)$ because

$$
33=5\cdot 6+3.
$$

Therefore, the residue of $33$ modulo $6$ is $3.$

**Method 2**

We can use the subtraction property:

$$
\begin{aligned}33 & ≡33-0 &  & (\text{mod}\,6) \\  & ≡33-5\cdot 6 &  & (\text{mod}\,6) \\  & ≡33-30 &  & (\text{mod}\,6) \\  & ≡3 &  & (\text{mod}\,6)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the residue of $33$ modulo $6$ is $3.$

The residue of $-28$ modulo $3$ is the integer $0\le r<3$ such that

$$
-28≡r\,(\text{mod}\,3).
$$

**Method 1**

To find the residue $r,$ we need to write $-28$ as an integer multiple of $3,$ plus the residue $r.$

We note that $-28≡2\,(\text{mod}\,3)$ because

$$
-28=(-10)\cdot 3+2.
$$

Therefore, the residue of $-28$ modulo $3$ is $2.$

**Method 2**

We can use the addition property:

$$
\begin{aligned}-28 & ≡-28+0 &  & (\text{mod}\,3) \\  & ≡-28+10\cdot 3 &  & (\text{mod}\,3) \\  & ≡-28+30 &  & (\text{mod}\,3) \\  & ≡2 &  & (\text{mod}\,3)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the residue of $-28$ modulo $3$ is $2.$

The residue of $-54$ modulo $7$ is the integer $0\le r<7$ such that

$$
-54≡r\,(\text{mod}\,7).
$$

**Method 1**

To find the residue $r,$ we need to write $-54$ as an integer multiple of $7,$ plus the residue $r.$

We note that $-54≡2\,(\text{mod}\,7)$ because

$$
-54=(-8)\cdot 7+2.
$$

Therefore, the residue of $-54$ modulo $7$ is $2.$

**Method 2**

We can use the addition property:

$$
\begin{aligned}-54 & ≡-54+0 &  & (\text{mod}\,7) \\  & ≡-54+8\cdot 7 &  & (\text{mod}\,7) \\  & ≡-54+56 &  & (\text{mod}\,7) \\  & ≡2 &  & (\text{mod}\,7)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the residue of $-54$ modulo $7$ is $2.$

questions.problem:
Let $a$ be a positive integer. Construct an expression that gives the last digit of $15a.$

$$
{{field-1}}{{field-2}}{{field-3}}
$$
questions.worked_solution:
Let $b=15a.$ Note that $b$ is positive. Now, let ${d}_{3},$ ${d}_{2},$ and ${d}_{1}$ be the last three digits of the number $b:$ 

$$
b=…{d}_{3}{d}_{2}{d}_{1}
$$

Then, $b$ can be written in expanded form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}b & =⋯+100{d}_{3}+10{d}_{2}+{d}_{1} \\  & =10(⋯+10{d}_{3}+{d}_{2})+{d}_{1}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute the residue of $b$ modulo $10:$

$$
\begin{aligned}b & ≡10(⋯+10{d}_{3}+{d}_{2})+{d}_{1} &  & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡0\cdot (⋯+10{d}_{3}+{d}_{2})+{d}_{1} &  & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡0+{d}_{1} &  & (\text{mod}\,10) \\  & ≡{d}_{1} &  & (\text{mod}\,10)\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that ${d}_{1}$ is the last digit of $b.$

Finally, since $b=15a,$ and 

$$
15≡5\,(\text{mod}\,10)
$$

we have the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}b & ≡{d}_{1} &  & (\text{mod}\,10) \\ 15a & ≡{d}_{1} &  & (\text{mod}\,10) \\ 5a & ≡{d}_{1} &  & (\text{mod}\,10)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the expression that gives the last digit of $15a$ is the following:

$$
5a\,\text{mod}\,10
$$
